act: Payment of Wages Act, 1936 & State Shops & Commercial Establishments Acts
title: Unpaid Wages, Full & Final Settlement (FnF) Withholding & Notice Pay
summary: Employers cannot unlawfully withhold earned wages, bonus, or statutory benefits upon resignation or termination. Full & Final Settlement (FnF) must typically be cleared within 7 to 30 days of the last working day (or 2 working days under the Code on Wages).
key_provisions: Wages must be paid by the 7th or 10th of the following month.
An employer cannot withhold experience/relieving letters or earned salary as leverage in contractual disputes.
Unauthorized deductions from salary are illegal under Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act.
If the employee has served the agreed notice period or agreed to notice buyout, the employer must clear all dues including accrued leave encashment and gratuity (if eligible).
remedy: 1. Send a formal written demand email/letter to HR and Senior Management citing Payment of Wages Act and Shops & Establishments Act, giving 7 working days. 2. File a formal complaint before the Regional Labour Commissioner / Conciliation Officer. 3. File a summary recovery suit under Section 33C(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act or local Shops & Establishment Authority.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act)
title: Workplace Harassment Protection & POSH Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)
summary: Statutory right of women to a safe working environment free from sexual harassment, unwelcome physical contact, sexually colored remarks, or implicit threats to employment status.
key_provisions: Every establishment with 10 or more employees MUST constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) headed by a senior woman employee and including an independent NGO member.
Complaint can be submitted within 3 months of the incident (extendable by another 3 months upon justification).
During inquiry, the aggrieved woman can request interim relief: transfer, up to 3 months paid leave (in addition to normal leave), or restraining the respondent from reporting on her appraisal.
Inquiry must be concluded within 90 days, and employer must implement recommendations within 60 days.
Identity of complainant and proceedings are strictly confidential under Section 16 (breach attracts penalties).
remedy: Submit written complaint (6 copies with supporting evidence/witness list) to the Presiding Officer of the ICC. If no ICC exists or employer is the respondent, submit complaint to the District Officer / Local Complaints Committee (LCC) or file via the SHe-Box portal (shebox.nic.in).

title: Maternity Leave, Pay Rights & Protection Against Dismissal
summary: Every woman who has worked for at least 80 days in an establishment of 10+ employees is entitled to 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave. It is unlawful to dismiss or discharge a woman employee during maternity leave.
key_provisions: Entitlement to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave (up to 8 weeks before delivery).
Section 12 makes it strictly unlawful for an employer to terminate, discharge, or vary conditions of service of a woman during her absence on maternity leave.
Establishments with 50 or more employees must provide a crèche facility within prescribed distance.
Work from home option may be mutually agreed after the 26-week period.
remedy: Issue legal notice to employer citing Section 12 of the Maternity Benefit Act. File complaint with the Chief Inspector of Factories / Labour Inspector.

act: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 & State Shops & Establishments Acts
title: Wrongful / Illegal Termination and Retrenchment Safeguards
summary: Protection against arbitrary termination without notice, cause, or mandatory retrenchment compensation.
key_provisions: Workmen with continuous service of 1 year cannot be retrenched without 1 month written notice (or pay in lieu) and retrenchment compensation (15 days average pay for every completed year of service).
Termination on fabricated charges without a domestic inquiry violating principles of natural justice can be set aside with back wages.
Shops & Establishments Acts generally mandate minimum 30 days notice or 30 days salary in lieu of notice for non-workmen.
remedy: Issue legal notice challenging the termination as illegal. File an Industrial Dispute before the Labour Conciliation Officer under Section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act.
